mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLK 350 engine reliable? What problems should I watch for?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272 V6 is a smooth and powerful engine, but early production units (2005-2007) suffer from a well-documented balance shaft sprocket defect. Later models (2007-onwards) are more reliable. Balance shaft sprocket wear affects 2005-2007 models - check engine serial number. Fault codes P0016/P0017 indicate timing correlation issues. Swirl flap linkage failure can cause loss of power below 1,800 rpm. Crankshaft position sensor failure causes stalling when hot. 2007+ facelift engines have hardened sprockets and are generally safe.

mainEntity.name: What is the M272 balance shaft problem on the Mercedes CLK 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272 V6 engine has a balance shaft sprocket made from soft metal that wears prematurely. As the sprocket teeth wear, the timing chain becomes slack, causing incorrect camshaft timing. Affects CLK 350 (2005-2007, M272 engines below serial #468933). Symptoms: check engine light with P0016/P0017 codes, rattling on startup. Repair requires specialist disassembly - engine-out job on many models. 2007+ facelift engines have hardened sprockets and are safe. Warning: Ignoring the rattle and codes can lead to timing chain jumping, valve damage, and complete engine destruction.

mainEntity.name: What causes loss of power on my Mercedes CLK 350 with no warning lights?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common culprits include snapped intake manifold swirl flap linkage rods or failed crankshaft position sensors. Plastic intake manifold linkage rods snap - £45 repair kit fixes it. Cam sensors can fail without storing permanent codes. Check VIN online to confirm if your engine is in the affected balance shaft range. Loss of power below 1,800 rpm is a classic swirl flap symptom.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLK 350 engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained M272 V6 engines regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. If the balance shaft has been replaced with a hardened sprocket, the engine is effectively bulletproof. M272: 150k-200k+ miles with regular servicing. Balance shaft replacement with hardened sprocket extends life indefinitely. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes CLK 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a CLK 350 worth £3,300-£5,000, specialist engine replacement at £1,900-£3,100 is worthwhile if the body and interior are in excellent condition. However, if the car has rust, electrical issues, or poor bodywork, consider scrapping it. A clean, well-maintained CLK 350 is worth saving. Rebuilt M272 with hardened sprockets costs £1,900-£3,100 supply only. Compare against £5,000-£8,000 main dealer new engine quotes. If the car has other major issues, replacement may not be cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: What is the 7G-TRONIC conductor plate problem on the CLK 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 7G-TRONIC transmission in the CLK 350 can suffer from conductor plate failure, causing the gearbox to enter limp mode. Symptoms: gearbox stuck in gear, harsh shifting, transmission warning light. Often mistaken for engine failure. Specialist conductor plate replacement costs £550-£850. Far cheaper than any engine work - don't replace the engine until the gearbox has been diagnosed.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLK 350 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLK 350 arrived with the C209 facelift in 2005, powered by the M272 E35 3.5-litre V6 - the most powerful non-AMG V6 ever fitted to the CLK. Producing 272 hp and 350 Nm of torque, it could sprint from 0-62 mph in just 6.4 seconds, making it the definitive grand tourer of the CLK range.

2007 - Early M272 engines affected by balance shaft sprocket defect
Production engine update: balance shaft issue resolved from mid-2007
2009 - CLK 350 available in coupé (C209) and cabriolet (A209) body styles
CLK production ends; M272 engine continues in other Mercedes models

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLK 350 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes CLK 350 is powered by the M272 3.5-litre V6 - a smooth and powerful engine that defined the CLK's grand touring character. However, early production units (2005-2007) suffer from a well-documented balance shaft sprocket defect that can lead to catastrophic engine failure. Later models are more reliable but can still experience swirl flap linkage failure and crankshaft position sensor issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Balance Shaft Sprocket Failure - The M272's Defining Weakness
problems.rootCause: A manufacturing defect in the balance shaft sprocket - the material is too soft and wears prematurely. As the sprocket teeth wear, the timing chain becomes slack, causing incorrect camshaft timing. All early M272 engines are potentially affected, with engines built after August 2007 considered safe.

repairOptions.tier: Full Timing Chain & Balance Shaft Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of balance shaft sprocket with hardened unit, timing chain, tensioners, guides. Engine-out job on many models.
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-100k miles if caught before catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement engine with upgraded balance shaft components, bench tested, supply & fit, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles or if timing has jumped and valve damage has occurred

problems.recommendation: The balance shaft issue is the single most significant problem affecting the CLK 350. If you're buying a pre-2008 CLK 350, check the engine serial number to confirm if it's in the affected range. If you own one and have P0016/P0017 codes, don't delay - specialist repair at £2,000-£2,500 is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. For cars with high mileage or other issues, a rebuilt unit with hardened sprockets offers peace of mind.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M272 Mercedes CLK 350 engine prices

problems.h4: Swirl Flap Linkage Failure - Loss of Power and Hesitation
problems.rootCause: The plastic linkage rods in the intake manifold swirl flap system break, causing the flaps to stick. This results in loss of power, hesitation below 1,800 rpm, and increased fuel consumption. The engine management light may illuminate with codes related to intake manifold runner control.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace broken linkage rods with upgraded metal components
Replace complete intake manifold with swirl flaps
repairOptions.longevity: Required if flaps themselves are damaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement engine with new intake manifold, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if flap debris has entered cylinders

problems.recommendation: Loss of power and hesitation below 1,800 rpm are classic symptoms of swirl flap linkage failure. A £150-£300 repair kit with metal linkage rods is the definitive fix. If the flaps themselves are damaged, a replacement intake manifold at £500-£900 is required. Catch it early - flap debris in the cylinders can cause catastrophic engine damage.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for M272 swirl flap repair for your Mercedes CLK 350

problems.h4: Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure - Intermittent Stalling
problems.rootCause: The crankshaft position sensor can fail due to heat cycling, causing internal wiring to break. Symptoms include the engine stalling when hot and difficulty restarting after 5-15 minutes. No fault codes are often stored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect wiring harness, camshaft sensors, and ECU connections
repairOptions.longevity: Required if CPS replacement doesn't resolve the issue

problems.recommendation: If your CLK 350 stalls when hot and won't restart for 5-15 minutes, start with the crankshaft position sensor - it's a £150-£300 specialist fix. The M272 engine is otherwise robust, and with proper maintenance, can exceed 150,000 miles.
